sentences.text: This genus is known from a nearly complete skeleton that includes a preserved skull.
It was a relatively small pterosaur similar in size and shape to Sordes, with a skull measuring 43 mm and a wingspan of at least 32 cm.
The only known fossil is a fully complete skeleton preserved in articulation within a single slab and a counter-slab.
Researchers suggest Jianchangopterus likely ate insects, unlike most of its contemporaries which ate fish.
The holotype was uncovered at the Linglongta locality in Jianchang County, Liaoning Province, China, from the Tiaojishan Formation.
Lü Junchang and Bo Xue named the genus in 2011 after Jianchang County and the type species, Jianchangopterus zhaoianus, was named in honor of Zhao Limin.
The holotype specimen is stored at the Yizhou Museum with the catalog number YHK-0931.
The genus is classified in the family Rhamphorhynchidae and the subfamily Scaphognathinae based on shared traits such as a short skull, short wing finger, long fifth toe, and long ulna.
It is considered a close relative of Sordes, Scaphognathus, Harpactognathus, and Fenghuangopterus.

The fossil dates to the Callovian-Oxfordian age of the Middle-Late Jurassic, approximately 159 million years ago, though the time range extends from the Bathonian to the Kimmeridgian, between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago.
The environment featured forests surrounding large lakes near active volcanoes, where volcanic ash aided fossil preservation, and the climate was likely subtropical to temperate, warm, and humid.
